before.paraphrase: Himavat tells Pārvatī of the vow practiced by Candraṅgada and his wife Indumatī. The king rules Karṇa city in Mālava, knows Vedas and śāstras, sacrifices and gives generously, and has a brilliant court. Verse 3 prints aṇimādiguṇāpeta; its capacity implication is withheld instead of silently changing it to guṇopeta. Indumatī is virtuous, serves her husband and parents-in-law, handles household duties and worships gods and guests. Ministers strongly urge the king to abandon the grievously sinful killing involved in hunting.
before.verification_notes: Direct Sanskrit body reading; not independent edition verification. Uncertain Sanskrit clauses identified separately.

after.paraphrase: Himavat tells Pārvatī of the vow practiced by Candraṅgada and his wife Indumatī. The king rules Karṇa city in Mālava, knows Vedas and śāstras, sacrifices and gives generously, and has a brilliant court. Verse 3 prints aṇimādiguṇāpeta: literally free from qualities such as aṇimā. The printed negative qualifier is retained, without emending it to guṇopeta or attributing miraculous perfections. Indumatī is virtuous, serves her husband and parents-in-law, handles household duties and worships gods and guests. Ministers strongly urge the king to abandon the grievously sinful killing involved in hunting.
after.verification_notes: Direct Sanskrit body reading; not independent edition verification. Uncertain Sanskrit clauses identified separately. Root and a second author checked the printed qualifier53.3 and Monier-Williams apeta, free-from sense in compounds (https://sanskrit.uohyd.ac.in/SKT/MW/12.html).
